items.a: Digital marketing is promoting a business through online channels: search engines (SEO and Google Ads), social media (LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube), email and WhatsApp marketing, content (blogs, videos), and websites / landing pages. It is measurable: you can track who saw, clicked, enquired and converted.

items.q: How to make a marketing plan?
items.a:
Marketing plan steps:
1. Goal: e.g. 50 qualified leads per month or 20 percent more revenue.
2. Target audience: industry, company size, role, location, pain points.
3. Positioning: why us (USP), key message.
4. Channels: LinkedIn, Google, email, WhatsApp, events, referrals.
5. Content calendar: what to post, when.
6. Budget per channel.
7. KPIs: leads, cost per lead, conversion rate, revenue.
8. Review monthly and shift budget to what works.

items.q: How to market a staffing company?

items.a:
Marketing a staffing company:
• LinkedIn: founders and recruiters post hiring insights, salary trends, success stories; connect with HR heads and founders.
• Cold email and calling to HR / TA heads of growing companies (funding news, job posts are signals).
• Case studies: "Closed 40 developer roles in 30 days for X".
• Website with clear services, industries and a contact form.
• Google Business Profile and local SEO.
• Referrals from happy clients and candidates.
• HR events, webinars and associations (NHRD, SHRM).

Lead generation methods: LinkedIn outreach and content, cold email campaigns with personalised messages, Google Ads on high-intent keywords, SEO blogs, landing pages with a clear offer, webinars, partnerships, referrals, events and trade shows, and directory listings (Justdial, IndiaMART, Clutch). Capture every lead in the CRM with source, and follow up within 24 hours, since speed matters most.

items.q: How to use LinkedIn for marketing?
items.a: LinkedIn tips: complete the company page and personal profiles (clear headline: what you do and for whom); post 3 to 5 times a week; mix content types (tips, case studies, behind-the-scenes, polls, short videos, carousels); write a strong first line; reply to comments quickly; send 20 to 30 personalised connection requests a day to your target audience; use LinkedIn Sales Navigator for prospecting; and run LinkedIn Ads only once you have a proven offer.

items.q: How to make a social media content calendar?
items.a: Content calendar: choose 3 to 4 content pillars (e.g. tips, success stories, company culture, offers). Plan a month ahead in a sheet with date, platform, pillar, topic, caption, creative, CTA and status. Example weekly mix: Mon tip, Tue job openings, Wed case study, Thu team / culture, Fri industry news or poll. Reuse one idea across platforms in different formats.

Instagram tips: post Reels 3 to 4 times a week (hook in the first 2 seconds, 15 to 30 seconds long, trending audio), use carousels for tips, post Stories daily (polls, Q&A), use 5 to 10 relevant hashtags, write clear captions with a CTA, reply to DMs and comments fast, collaborate with creators, and check Insights weekly to repeat what works.

items.a: SEO (Search Engine Optimization) means improving your website so it ranks higher on Google for free. Basics: research keywords your customers search; one page per main keyword with it in the title, heading and URL; helpful, original content; fast mobile-friendly site; internal links; backlinks from trusted sites; Google Business Profile for local search; and Google Search Console to track rankings. SEO takes 3 to 6 months to show results.

Google Ads shows your ad when people search specific keywords, and you pay per click (PPC). Steps: pick high-intent keywords (e.g. "staffing agency in Pune"), write ads with the keyword and a clear offer, send traffic to a focused landing page, set a daily budget, add negative keywords to block irrelevant searches, and track conversions (form fills, calls). Start small, review weekly, and keep only the keywords that bring leads.

Email marketing tips: build a clean list (only people who opted in, or carefully researched B2B contacts); personalise the subject and first line; keep it short (under 120 words) with one clear CTA; send from a warmed-up domain; follow up 2 to 3 times over 2 weeks; track open, click and reply rates; and always include an unsubscribe option. Good benchmarks: 40 percent+ open rate, 3 to 8 percent reply rate for cold B2B.

items.q: Give a cold email template for a staffing client
items.a:
Cold email template:
Subject: Hiring <role> faster at <Company>?
Hi <Name>, I noticed <Company> is hiring for <role / team>. We help companies like <similar client> close <role> positions in 2 to 3 weeks with pre-screened candidates, with a free replacement guarantee. Would a quick 15-minute call this week be useful? I can share 2 to 3 sample profiles first.
Regards, <Your name>, <Company>, <Phone>

WhatsApp marketing: use WhatsApp Business (catalogue, quick replies, labels, auto greeting); for bulk messages use the official WhatsApp Business API through a provider, with approved templates; only message people who opted in; use broadcast lists and Status for updates; keep messages short with one CTA; and track replies. Avoid spam, since users can block and report you and the number can be banned.

items.q: What marketing KPIs should we track?
items.a: Key marketing KPIs: leads generated, cost per lead (CPL), lead-to-customer conversion rate, customer acquisition cost (CAC), return on ad spend (ROAS), website traffic and conversion rate, email open / click / reply rates, social reach and engagement rate, and revenue influenced by marketing. Track by channel so you can move budget to the best-performing ones.

items.q: How to plan a marketing campaign?
items.a: Campaign planning: define one goal and KPI; choose the audience; write the offer and key message; select channels; create assets (posts, ads, emails, landing page); set budget and timeline; set up tracking (UTM links, conversion tracking); launch; monitor daily for the first week; A/B test headlines and creatives; and do a post-campaign review of results and learnings.

A UTM link is a normal URL with tags that tell Google Analytics where a visitor came from. Example: https://site.com/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=nov_hiring. Use source (platform), medium (type such as social, email, cpc) and campaign (name). Use Google's Campaign URL Builder and keep the naming consistent.

Branding is how people recognise and feel about your company: name, logo, colours, fonts, tone of voice, values and the experience you deliver. Strong branding is consistent everywhere (website, social media, proposals, email signatures, office). Create a simple brand guide so every team member uses the same logo, colours and messaging.

USP (Unique Selling Proposition) is the clear reason a customer should choose you over competitors. Formula: We help <target customer> achieve <result> through <unique method>, unlike <alternatives>. For a staffing firm, for example: "Pre-screened tech candidates in 7 days, with a 90-day free replacement." Use it in your website headline, pitch and ads.

Content marketing means creating useful content (blogs, videos, guides, case studies, newsletters, posts) that attracts and educates your target customers, building trust so they buy from you. Content ideas for staffing and HR: salary guides, hiring trend reports, interview tips, JD templates, case studies, and "how we hired X in Y days" stories.

items.q: What makes a good landing page?
items.a: A good landing page has one goal: a clear headline with the benefit, a short sub-headline, 3 to 5 benefit bullets, social proof (client logos, testimonials, numbers), a simple form (name, phone, email, company, maximum 4 to 5 fields), one strong CTA button, fast loading on mobile, and no distracting menu links. Test different headlines and CTAs.

items.q: How much should we spend on marketing?
items.a: A common guideline is 5 to 10 percent of revenue for established businesses and 10 to 20 percent for fast-growing ones. Start with a test budget per channel, measure cost per lead and cost per customer, and scale only channels where the customer's lifetime value is at least 3 times the acquisition cost.

items.q: How to create a customer persona?
items.a: A customer persona is a profile of your ideal buyer: job title, industry, company size, location, goals, pain points, objections, where they spend time online, and what influences their decisions. Example for staffing: "HR Head, 200 to 1000 employee IT company, struggles to hire developers fast, active on LinkedIn, values quality and speed over price." Build it from real customer conversations.

Festive campaign ideas: themed greeting posts with your brand colours, limited-time offers (e.g. a reduced fee for hires closed this month), employee celebration posts and videos, client thank-you emails or gifts, contests and quizzes, a year-end hiring outlook post, and WhatsApp greetings to clients and candidates. Plan creatives 2 weeks early.

items.a: Employer branding is your reputation as a place to work. Improve it by sharing employee stories, culture and events on LinkedIn and Instagram, keeping a good Glassdoor / AmbitionBox rating, a careers page with benefits and growth paths, fast and respectful hiring processes, and encouraging employees to share their experiences. Strong employer branding reduces hiring cost and time.

items.q: What should a monthly marketing report include?
items.a: Monthly marketing report: summary of goals vs results; leads by channel; cost per lead and spend by channel; conversions and revenue influenced; website traffic and top pages; social media growth and top posts; email results; what worked, what didn't; and next month's plan and budget changes. Keep it to 1 to 2 pages with simple charts.
